content.text: I changed one file, `solution/util.py`, and the visible suite now passes (2 passed). The bug was in `_parse_class`: it parsed range expressions like `a-z` correctly and stored them in a `ranges` list, but the `match` function it returns only checked `ch in chars` and never looked at `ranges`. So any character covered by a range didn't count as a match. That's why `[a-z]x` failed to match `mx`, and why `[!a-c]x` wrongly matched `ax`, since the negation flipped a miss that should have been a hit. The fix makes `match` count a character as a hit if it's in `chars` or falls inside any of the stored `(lo, hi)` ranges. The existing rules still apply: `/` never matches a class, and `!` negation is applied after the range check.

result: I changed one file, `solution/util.py`, and the visible suite now passes (2 passed). The bug was in `_parse_class`: it parsed range expressions like `a-z` correctly and stored them in a `ranges` list, but the `match` function it returns only checked `ch in chars` and never looked at `ranges`. So any character covered by a range didn't count as a match. That's why `[a-z]x` failed to match `mx`, and why `[!a-c]x` wrongly matched `ax`, since the negation flipped a miss that should have been a hit. The fix makes `match` count a character as a hit if it's in `chars` or falls inside any of the stored `(lo, hi)` ranges. The existing rules still apply: `/` never matches a class, and `!` negation is applied after the range check.
